source_text: Inter carnis alimenta, benedicti martyres designati, quae vobis et domina mater ecclesia de uberibus suis et singuli fratres de opibus suis propriis in carcerem subministrant, capite aliquid et a nobis, quod faciat ad spiritum quoque educandum. Carnem enim saginari et spiritum esurire non prodest. Immo si quod infirmum est curatur, aeque quod infirmius est neglegi non debet. Nec tantus ego sum, ut vos alloquar. Verumtamen et gladiatores perfectissimos non tantum magistri et praepositi sui, sed etiam idiotae et supervacue quique adhortantur de longinquo, ut saepe de ipso populo dictata suggesta profuerint. Inprimis ergo, benedicti, nolite contristare spiritum sanctum, qui vobiscum introiit carcerem. Si enim non vobiscum nunc introisset, nec vos illic hodie fuissetis. Et ideo date operam, ut illic vobiscum perseveret: ita vos inde perducat ad dominum. Domus quidem diaboli est et carcer, in qua familiam suam continet. Sed vos ideo in carcerem pervenistis, ut illum etiam in domo sua conculcetis. Iam enim foris congressi conculcaveratis. Non ergo dicat: In meo sunt, temptabo illos vilibus odiis, defectionibus aut inter se dissensionibus. Fugiat conspectum vestrum et in ima sua deliteseat contractus et torpens, tamquam coluber exeantatus aut effumigatus. Nec illi tam bene sit in suo regno, ut vos commitat, sed inveniat munitos et concordia armatos, quia pax vestra bellum est illi. Quam pacem quidam in ecclesia non habentes a martyribus in earcere exorare consueverunt. Et ideo eam propterea in vobis habere et fovere et custodire debetis, ut, si forte, et aliis praestare possitis.
thought_title: The prison as the devil's house to be conquered
orientation: Tertullian opens his treatise by addressing the imprisoned Christians, urging them to care for the spirit as well as the flesh and to preserve peace among themselves so the Holy Spirit remains with them in the prison.
pass_a_gloss: Among the nourishments of the flesh, blessed designated martyrs, which both the lady mother church from her breasts and individual brothers from their own resources supply to you in prison, accept also something from us, which may serve for nourishing the spirit too. For it is not profitable for the flesh to be fattened and the spirit to hunger. Rather, if what is weak is cared for, equally what is weaker ought not to be neglected. Nor am I so great that I should address you. Nevertheless, even the most accomplished gladiators are exhorted not only by their trainers and overseers but also by laymen and all sorts of superfluous people from a distance, so that often suggestions dictated from the crowd itself have been of use. First of all, then, blessed ones, do not grieve the Holy Spirit, who entered the prison with you. For if he had not now entered with you, you would not have been there today. And therefore take care that he may remain there with you: so may he lead you from there to the Lord. The prison is indeed the house of the devil, in which he keeps his household. But you have come into prison for this purpose, that you may trample him even in his own house. For you had already trampled him by fighting outside. Let him not say, then: They are in my domain, I will test them with cheap hatreds, with defections or with dissensions among themselves. Let him flee from your sight and hide away in his depths, shriveled and sluggish, like a snake that has been charmed or smoked out. Nor let it be so well for him in his own kingdom that he may set you against each other, but let him find you fortified and armed with concord, because your peace is war to him. This peace some who do not have it in the church have been accustomed to beg from the martyrs in prison. And therefore you ought to have it and cherish it and guard it in yourselves for this reason, that you may be able, if perhaps, to supply it to others also.

choices.why: Keeps the legal/technical sense of designati as those marked out or appointed for martyrdom, not yet crowned.
Preserves the honorific domina and the maternal metaphor of the church nursing her children.

choices.english: laymen and all sorts of superfluous people
choices.why: Idiotae means non-specialists or laymen; supervacue quique conveys the dismissive tone of people with no business being there.

choices.english: do not grieve the Holy Spirit
choices.why: Echoes Ephesians 4:30 wording and keeps the imperative force of nolite with the infinitive.
rejected: do not sadden the Holy Spirit
do not make the Holy Spirit sorrowful

choices.why: Vilibus means cheap, worthless, or base; the devil's weapons are contemptible.

choices.english: a snake that has been charmed or smoked out
choices.why: Keeps the vivid image of a snake rendered powerless by charming or smoking, matching the passive participles.
rejected: a snake driven out by spells or smoke

pass_b_english: Blessed designated martyrs, while the lady mother church from her breasts and individual brothers from their own resources supply you in prison with food for the flesh, accept something from us as well, to nourish the spirit. For it does no good to fatten the flesh while the spirit hungers. Indeed, if what is weak is cared for, what is weaker still should not be neglected. Nor am I so great that I should address you. Yet even the most accomplished gladiators are encouraged not only by their trainers and managers but also by laymen and all sorts of superfluous people shouting from a distance, so that suggestions dictated from the crowd itself have often proved useful.

First of all, then, blessed ones, do not grieve the Holy Spirit, who entered the prison with you. For if He had not entered with you now, you would not be there today. So make every effort that He may remain there with you, and so lead you from there to the Lord. The prison is indeed the devil's house, where he keeps his household. But you have come into the prison precisely so that you may trample him even in his own house. You had already trampled him outside.

So let him not say: "They are in my territory. I will tempt them with cheap hatreds, with defections, or with dissensions among themselves." Let him flee from your sight and hide away in his depths, shriveled and numb, like a snake that has been stripped or smoked out. Let it not go so well for him in his own kingdom that he brings you into conflict. Instead, let him find you fortified and armed with harmony, because your peace is war against him. Some who do not have this peace in the church have been accustomed to beg for it from martyrs in prison. And so you ought to have it, cherish it, and guard it among yourselves for this reason: so that you may perhaps be able to supply it to others as well.

problems.quote: You had already fought him outside and trampled him.
problems.why: The Latin mentions only that they have already trampled him outside; it does not say they fought him.
problems.fix: You had already trampled him outside.

problems.quote: like a snake that has been charmed or smoked out
problems.why: The Latin describes a snake that has been stripped/emptied (or exsanguinated), not charmed.
problems.fix: like a snake that has been stripped or smoked out

problems.why: The Latin says the provision comes from us (the community), not from the speaker alone.
problems.ruling: "a nobis" is plural 'from us,' not singular 'from me'; speaker represents community, misleading to make it personal.

edits.old: You had already fought him outside and trampled him.
edits.new: You had already trampled him outside.

edits.old: like a snake that has been charmed or smoked out
edits.new: like a snake that has been stripped or smoked out

edits.old: accept something from me as well
edits.new: accept something from us as well

fixed: Removed 'fought him' because the Latin 'congressi conculcaveratis' only says they trampled him outside.
Changed 'charmed' to 'stripped' because 'exeantatus' means emptied/stripped, not charmed.
Changed 'from me' to 'from us' because the Latin 'a nobis' is plural.

last_rejected.why: Missing 'the devil' as speaker; English hides whose words these are per voices brief
last_rejected.fix: So let the devil not say
last_rejected.ruling: Context makes “him” clearly refer to the devil; omission does not change meaning.

last_rejected.why: English omits 'propterea' (for this very reason/for that reason), losing emphasis
last_rejected.fix: And so for this very reason you ought to have it
last_rejected.ruling: “For this reason” conveys propterea’s sense; omission of the word itself is not a meaning loss.
